419279 read(10, "# Semantic Search Quality Evaluation\n\nThis evaluation measures the quality of semantic search queries generated by Forge using an LLM-as-judge approach.\n\n## Quick Start\n\n### Test Your Queries Manually\n\nBefore running the full eval, test your queries to get immediate feedback:\n\n```bash\n# Interactive mode\nnpx tsx benchmarks/evals/semantic_search_quality/test_queries.ts\n\n# Non-interactive mode\nnpx tsx benchmarks/evals/semantic_search_quality/test_queries.ts \\\n  \"retry mechanism with exponential backoff\" \\\n  \"I need to find the implementation code for retry logic\"\n```\n\nThe query tester provides:\n- Detailed scores for embedding and reranking queries\n- Specific strengths and weaknesses\n- Actionable suggestions for improvement\n- Differentiation analysis\n\n### Run the Full Evaluation\n\n```bash\n# Run the entire semantic search quality eval\nnpm run eval semantic_search_quality\n\n# Run with specific parallelism\nnpm run eval semantic_search_quality -- --parallelism 10\n\n# Run with specific model\nnpm run eval semantic_search_quality -- --model \"anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5\"\n```\n\n## Purpose\n\nThe semantic search feature uses two types of queries:\n1. **Embedding Query (`query`)**: Converted to vector embeddings for semantic similarity search\n2. **Reranking Query (`use_case`)**: Used by the reranker to filter results based on intent\n\nThis eval verifies that:\n- Queries are well-formed and contain sufficient context\n- The two queries are different and serve distinct purposes\n- Results match the user's intent (implementation vs docs vs tests, etc.)\n- Correct file types are returned based on intent\n- Unwanted file types are avoided\n\n## How It Works\n\n### 1. Test Execution\nThe eval runs various semantic search tasks covering different intents:\n- **Implementation**: Find actual code, not documentation\n- **Flow Understanding**: Understand how systems work\n- **Architecture**: Understand structural design\n- **Tests**: Find test examples and fixtures\n- **Documentation**: Find docs and guides\n- **Debugging**: Investigate issues\n- **Modification**: Find code to modify\n- **Configuration**: Find config files and schemas\n\n### 2. LLM Judge Evaluation\nAfter each task, an LLM judge (Gemini 3 Pro) evaluates:\n\n#### Query Quality (40 points)\n- **Embedding Query (15pts)**: Domain terms, technical context, behavior description\n- **Reranking Query (15pts)**: Intent clarity, context about WHY, specificity\n- **Query Differentiation (10pts)**: Queries serve different purposes\n\n#### Result Relevance (60 points)\n- **Intent Matching (25pts)**: Results match the stated intent\n- **File Type Accuracy (20pts)**: Correct file types returned\n- **Avoidance Compliance (15pts)**: Unwanted file types avoided\n\n#### Pass Criteria\n- Total score >= 70/100\n- No critical issues (e.g., identical queries, severe intent mismatch)\n\n### 3. Structured Output\nThe judge uses structured output (Zod schema) to provide:\n- Detailed scores for each dimension\n- Specific feedback on what's good/bad\n- List of critical issues\n- Overall pass/fail determination\n\n## Environment Variables\n\nRequired:\n- `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`: Path to Google Cloud service account JSON credentials file\n\nOr authenticate using `gcloud auth application-default login`.\n\nThe LLM judge uses Vertex AI to run Gemini 3 Pro. It supports Google's Application Default Credentials through the `google-auth-library`. The most common authentication method is to set the path to a JSON credentials file in the `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` environment variable.\n\n## Test Cases\n\nThe eval includes diverse test cases:\n\n### Implementation Queries\n```yaml\n- task: \"Find the retry mechanism with exponential backoff implementation\"\n  intent: \"implementation\"\n  expected_file_types: \"rust,typescript,javascript\"\n  should_avoid: \"markdown,txt,documentation\"\n```\n\n### Flow Understanding\n```yaml\n- task: \"How does the authentication flow work from request to response?\"\n  intent: \"flow_understanding\"\n  expected_file_types: \"rust,typescript\"\n  should_avoid: \"test,markdown\"\n```\n\n### Documentation\n```yaml\n- task: \"Find documentation on how to configure semantic search\"\n  intent: \"documentation\"\n  expected_file_types: \"markdown,txt\"\n  should_avoid: \"rust,typescript,javascript\"\n```\n\n## Interpreting Results\n\n### High Scores (>80)\nQueries are excellent - domain-specific, well-differentiated, and would return highly relevant results.\n\n### Medium Scores (60-80)\nQueries are functional but have room for improvement. Check feedback for specific suggestions.\n\n### Low Scores (<60)\nQueries have significant issues:\n- Too generic or vague\n- Embedding and reranking queries too similar\n- Intent mismatch\n- Would return wrong file types\n\n## Common Issues\n\n1. **Identical Queries**: Embedding and reranking queries are the same or too similar\n   - **Fix**: Make reranking query focus on intent, not just rephrasing\n\n2. **Generic Queries**: Lack domain-specific context\n   - **Fix**: Add technical terms, describe behavior, include framework names\n\n3. **Intent Mismatch**: Queries would return docs when implementation is needed\n   - **Fix**: Be explicit in reranking query about what type of code is needed\n\n4. **Poor Differentiation**: Both queries try to do the same thing\n   - **Fix**: Embedding = WHAT code does, Reranking = WHY you need it\n\n## Architecture\n\n```\ntask.yml\n\342\224\234\342\224\200\342\224\200 Runs Forge with semantic search task\n\342\224\234\342\224\200\342\224\200 Captures debug output (context.json)\n\342\224\224\342\224\200\342\224\200 Validates with llm_judge.ts\n    \342\224\234\342\224\200\342\224\200 Extracts sem_search calls\n    \342\224\234\342\224\200\342\224\200 Calls Gemini 3 Pro with structured output\n    \342\224\224\342\224\200\342\224\200 Returns evaluation with scores\n```\n\n## Extending the Eval\n\nTo add new test cases:\n\n1. Add to `task.yml` under `sources`:\n```yaml\n- task: \"Your task description\"\n  intent: \"implementation|flow_understanding|tests|documentation|debugging|modification|architecture|configuration\"\n  expected_file_types: \"comma,separated,extensions\"\n  should_avoid: \"comma,separated,extensions\"\n```\n\n2. Choose appropriate intent:\n   - `implementation`: Actual code implementation\n   - `flow_understanding`: Understanding how things work\n   - `architecture`: Structural/design understanding\n   - `tests`: Test files and fixtures\n   - `documentation`: Docs, README, guides\n   - `debugging`: Finding bugs/issues\n   - `modification`: Code to modify/extend\n   - `configuration`: Config files, schemas\n\n## Future Improvements\n\n- [ ] Add actual result verification (not just query quality)\n- [ ] Measure embedding quality directly\n- [ ] Test reranking effectiveness with real results\n- [ ] Add precision/recall metrics\n- [ ] Compare against human-labeled ground truth\n- [ ] Test edge cases (very short queries, multi-lingual code, etc.)\n", 6660) = 6660

This transformer recursively processes the\n/// schema to add this requirement.\n///\n/// # Example\n///\n/// Before normalization:\n/// ```json\n/// {\n///   \"type\": \"object\",\n///   \"properties\": { \"name\": { \"type\": \"string\" } }\n/// }\n/// ```\n///\n/// After normalization:\n/// ```json\n/// {\n///   \"type\": \"object\",\n///   \"properties\": { \"name\": { \"type\": \"string\" } },\n///   \"additionalProperties\": false\n/// }\n/// ```\npub struct EnforceStrictObjectSchema;\n\nimpl Transformer for EnforceStrictObjectSchema {\n    type Value = Request;\n\n    fn transform(&mut self, mut request: Self::Value) -> Self::Value {\n        if let Some(OutputFormat::JsonSchema { schema }) = request.output_format.take() {\n            // Convert schema to JSON value for normalization\n            if let Ok(mut schema_value) = serde_json::to_value(&schema) {\n                // Use non-strict mode (false) for Anthropic - only adds additionalProperties\n                enforce_strict_schema(&mut schema_value, false);\n\n                // Convert back to RootSchema\n                if let Ok(normalized_schema) = serde_json::from_value(schema_value) {\n                    request.output_format =\n                        Some(OutputFormat::JsonSchema { schema: normalized_schema });\n                } else {\n                    // If deserialization fails, keep the original schema\n                    request.output_format = Some(OutputFormat::JsonSchema { schema });\n                }\n            } else {\n                // If serialization fails, keep the original schema\n                request.output_format = Some(OutputFormat::JsonSchema { schema });\n            }\n        }\n\n        request\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use  #[allow(dead_code)]\n    struct TestResponse {\n        name: String,\n        nested: NestedObject,\n    }\n\n    #[derive(Deserialize, JsonSchema)]\n    #[allow(dead_code)]\n    struct NestedObject {\n        value: String,\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn test_normalize_output_schema_adds_additional_properties() {\n        let schema = schemars::schema_for!(TestResponse);\n        let fixture = Request::default().output_format(OutputFormat::JsonSchema { schema });\n\n        let actual = EnforceStrictObjectSchema.transform(fixture);\n\n        // Convert to JSON to check if additionalProperties was added\n        if let Some(OutputFormat::JsonSchema { schema }) = actual.output_format {\n            let schema_json = serde_json::to_value(&schema).unwrap();\n\n            // Check top-level schema\n            assert_eq!(\n                schema_json[\"additionalProperties\"],\n                serde_json::Value::Bool(false),\n                \"Top-level additionalProperties should be false\"\n            );\n\n            // Check nested object schema - it might be in definitions or $defs\n            if let Some(nested_schema) = schema_json\n Request;\n\n    fn transform(&mut self, mut request: Self::Value) -> Self::Value {\n        let regex = Regex::new(r\"[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]\").unwrap();\n\n        for message in &mut request.messages {\n .system\n            .as_ref()\n            .is_some_and(|messages| !messages.is_empty());\n\n        if let Some(system_messages) = request.system.as_mut() {\n            for message in = self.check_repeating_pattern(&all_signatures)?;\n\n        Some(count)\n    }\n\n    fn extract_tool_signatures(\n        &self,\n        conversation: &Conversation,\n    ) -> Vec<(ToolName, ToolCallArguments)> {\n        let assistant_messages = conversation\n            .context\n            .as_ref()\n            .map(|ctx| {\n                Self::extract_assistant_messages(ctx.messages.iter().map(|entry| &entry.message))\n            })\n            .unwrap_or_default();\n\n        assistant_messages\n            .iter()\n            .filter_map(|msg| msg.tool_calls.as_ref())\n            .flat_map(|calls| calls.iter())\n            .map(|call| (call.name.clone(), call.arguments.clone()))\n            .collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Checks for repeating patterns at the end of the sequence.\n    fn check_repeating_pattern<T>(&self, sequence: &[T]) -> Option<(usize, usize)>\n    where\n        T: Eq,\n    {\n        if sequence.is_empty() {\n            return None;\n        }\n\n        if sequence.len() < self.threshold {\n            return None;\n        }\n\n        for pattern_length in 1..sequence.len() {\n            let complete_repetitions =\n                self.count_recent_pattern_repetitions(sequence, pattern_length);\n\n            if complete_repetitions >= self.threshold {\n                let pattern_offset = complete_repetitions.checked_mul(pattern_length)?;\n                let pattern_start_idx = sequence.len().checked_sub(pattern_offset)?;\n\n                if sequence.get(pattern_start_idx).is_some() {\n                    return Some((pattern_start_idx, complete_repetitions));\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        None\n    }\n\n    /// Counts how many times a pattern of given length repeats at the END of\n    /// the sequence\n    ///\n    /// This works backwards from the most recent calls to find repeating\n    /// patterns, which allows detecting new patterns even if earlier\n    /// patterns existed. For example, in [1,2,3,1,2,3,4,5,4,5,4,5], this\n    /// will detect [4,5] repeating 3 times.\n    fn count_recent_pattern_repetitions<T>(&self, sequence: &[T], pattern_length: usize) -> usize\n    where\n        T: Eq,\n    {\n        if pattern_length == 0 || sequence.len() < pattern_length {\n            return 0;\n        }\n\n        // Start from the end and work backwards\n        let total_len = sequence.len();\n        let mut repetitions = 0;\n\n        // The pattern is defined by the last pattern_length elements\n        // For a partial match, we consider it as the start of a new repetition\n        let mut check_len = total_len;\n\n        // Special case: if total length is not evenly divisible by pattern_length,\n        // we have a partial match at the end\n        if !total_len.is_multiple_of(pattern_length) {\n            let partial_len = total_len % pattern_length;\n            // Check if the partial segment matches the start of what would be the pattern\n            // We need to look back to find what the pattern would be\n            if total_len < pattern_length + partial_len {\n                return 0;\n            }\n\n            let pattern_start = total_len - partial_len - pattern_length;\n            let pattern_end = pattern_start + pattern_length;\n            let partial_start = total_len - partial_len;\n\n            let Some(pattern) = sequence.get(pattern_start..pattern_end) else {\n                return 0;\n            };\n            let Some(partial) = sequence.get(partial_start..total_len) else {\n                return 0;\n            };\n            let Some(pattern_prefix) = pattern.get(..partial_len) else {\n                return 0;\n            };\n\n            if partial == pattern_prefix {\n                repetitions += 1;\n                check_len = total_len - partial_len;\n            } else {\n                // Partial doesn't match, no pattern\n                return 0;\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Now check complete repetitions working backwards\n        if check_len < pattern_length {\n            return repetitions;\n        }\n\n        // The pattern is the last complete chunk\n        let pattern_start = check_len - pattern_length;\n        let Some(pattern) = sequence.get(pattern_start..check_len) else {\n            return repetitions;\n        };\n        repetitions += 1; // Count the pattern itself\n\n        // Check backwards for more repetitions\n        let mut pos = pattern_start;\n        while pos >= pattern_length {\n            pos -= pattern_length;\n            let Some(chunk) = sequence.get(pos..pos + pattern_length) else {\n                break;\n            };\n\n            if chunk == pattern {\n                repetitions += 1;\n            } else {\n                // Pattern broken, stop counting\n                break;\n            }\n        }\n\n        repetitions\n    }\n\n    /// Extracts assistant messages from context messages\n    ///\n    /// Helper method to filter assistant messages from a conversation context\n    pub fn extract_assistant_messages<'a>(\n        messages: impl Iterator<Item = &'a   }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use forge_domain::{\n        Context, ContextMessage, ConversationId, MessageEntry, ToolCallArguments, ToolCallFull,\n    };\n    use When performing batch semantic searches, the same code node may appear in\n//! multiple queries with different scores. This module provides functionality\n//! to deduplicate results, keeping each node only in the query where it has\n//! the best score.\n\nuse std::cmp::Ordering;\nuse std::collections::HashMap;\n\nuse forge_domain::{Node, NodeId};\n\n/// Tracks the best score for a node across multiple queries.\n///\n/// Implements `Ord` to enable comparison based on score quality.\n/// Priority: relevance (higher is better) \342\206\222 distance (lower is better) \342\206\222\n/// similarity (higher is better) \342\206\222 query index (lower is better, tie-breaker).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\nstruct Score {\n    query_idx: usize,\n    relevance: Option<f32>,\n    distance: Option<f32>,\n}\n\nimpl Score {\n    /// Creates a new `BestScore` from a query index and search result.\n    fn new(query_idx: usize, result: &Node) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            query_idx,\n            relevance: result.relevance,\n            distance: result.distance,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Eq for Score {}\n\nimpl PartialOrd for Score {\n    fn partial_cmp(&self, other: &Self) -> Option<Ordering> {\n        Some(self.cmp(other))\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Ord for Score {\n    fn cmp(&self, other: &Self) -> Ordering {\n        /// Helper to compare two `Option<f32>` values (higher is better).\n        ///\n        /// # Returns\n        /// - `Some(Ordering)` if comparison is decisive\n        /// - `None` to continue to next comparison\n        fn compare(a: Option<f32>, b: Option<f32>) -> Option<Ordering> {\n            match (a, b) {\n                (Some(x), Some(y)) => match x.partial_cmp(&y)? {\n                    Ordering::Equal => None, // Continue to next comparison\n                    ord => Some(ord),\n                },\n                (Some(_), None) => Some(Ordering::Greater), // Having a value is better than None\n                (None, Some(_)) => Some(Ordering::Less),    // None is worse than having a value\n                (None, None) => None,                       // Continue to next comparison\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Compare in priority order: relevance \342\206\222 distance \342\206\222 similarity \342\206\222 query index\n        compare(self.relevance, other.relevance) // Higher relevance is better\n            .or_else(|| compare(other.distance, self.distance)) // Lower distance is better (flipped)\n            .unwrap_or_else(|| self.query_idx.cmp(&other.query_idx).reverse()) // Lower query index wins (first query wins)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Deduplicates code search results across multiple queries.\n///\n/// Each node appears only once across all query results, kept in the query\n/// where it has the highest score according to the `BestScore` ordering.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n/// * `results` - Vector of search results per query (will be modified in place)\n///\n/// # Errors\n/// Returns an error if node IDs cannot be extracted from results.\npub fn deduplicate_results(results: &mut [Vec<Node>]) {\n    // Track best score for each node_id across all queries\n    let mut best_scores: HashMap<NodeId, Score> = HashMap::new();\n\n    // First pass: find which query has the best score for each node\n    for (query_idx, query_results) in results.iter().enumerate() {\n        for result in query_results {\n            let current_score = Score::new(query_idx, result);\n            match best_scores.entry(result.node_id.clone()) {\n                std::collections::hash_map::Entry::Occupied(mut entry) => {\n                    if current_score > *entry.get() {\n                        entry.insert(current_score);\n                    }\n                }\n                std::collections::hash_map::Entry::Vacant(entry) => {\n                    entry.insert(current_score);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Second pass: remove duplicates, keeping only in the query with best score\n    for (query_idx, query_results) in results.iter_mut().enumerate() {\n        query_results.retain(|result| {\n            best_scores\n                .get(&result.node_id)\n                .is_none_or(|best| best.query_idx == query_idx)\n        });\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use forge_domain::{Node, NodeData};\n    use pretty_assertions::assert_eq;\n\n    use super::*;\n\n    /// Test fixture for creating a minimal When performing batch semantic searches, the same code node may appear in\n//! multiple queries with different scores. This module provides functionality\n//! to deduplicate results, keeping each node only in the query where it has\n//! the best score.\n\nuse std::cmp::Ordering;\nuse std::collections::HashMap;\n\nuse forge_domain::{Node, NodeId};\n\n/// Tracks the best score for a node across multiple queries.\n///\n/// Implements `Ord` to enable comparison based on score quality.\n/// Priority: relevance (higher is better) \342\206\222 distance (lower is better) \342\206\222\n/// similarity (higher is better) \342\206\222 query index (lower is better, tie-breaker).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\nstruct Score {\n    query_idx: usize,\n    relevance: Option<f32>,\n    distance: Option<f32>,\n}\n\nimpl Score {\n    /// Creates a new `BestScore` from a query index and search result.\n    fn new(query_idx: usize, result: &Node) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            query_idx,\n            relevance: result.relevance,\n            distance: result.distance,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Eq for Score {}\n\nimpl PartialOrd for Score {\n    fn partial_cmp(&self, other: &Self) -> Option<Ordering> {\n        Some(self.cmp(other))\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Ord for Score {\n    fn cmp(&self, other: &Self) -> Ordering {\n        /// Helper to compare two `Option<f32>` values (higher is better).\n        ///\n        /// # Returns\n        /// - `Some(Ordering)` if comparison is decisive\n        /// - `None` to continue to next comparison\n        fn compare(a: Option<f32>, b: Option<f32>) -> Option<Ordering> {\n            match (a, b) {\n                (Some(x), Some(y)) => match x.partial_cmp(&y)? {\n                    Ordering::Equal => None, // Continue to next comparison\n                    ord => Some(ord),\n                },\n                (Some(_), None) => Some(Ordering::Greater), // Having a value is better than None\n                (None, Some(_)) => Some(Ordering::Less),    // None is worse than having a value\n                (None, None) => None,                       // Continue to next comparison\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Compare in priority order: relevance \342\206\222 distance \342\206\222 similarity \342\206\222 query index\n        compare(self.relevance, other.relevance) // Higher relevance is better\n            .or_else(|| compare(other.distance, self.distance)) // Lower distance is better (flipped)\n            .unwrap_or_else(|| self.query_idx.cmp(&other.query_idx).reverse()) // Lower query index wins (first query wins)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Deduplicates code search results across multiple queries.\n///\n/// Each node appears only once across all query results, kept in the query\n/// where it has the highest score according to the `BestScore` ordering.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n/// * `results` - Vector of search results per query (will be modified in place)\n///\n/// # Errors\n/// Returns an error if node IDs cannot be extracted from results.\npub fn deduplicate_results(results: &mut [Vec<Node>]) {\n    // Track best score for each node_id across all queries\n    let mut best_scores: HashMap<NodeId, Score> = HashMap::new();\n\n    // First pass: find which query has the best score for each node\n    for (query_idx, query_results) in results.iter().enumerate() {\n        for result in query_results {\n            let current_score = Score::new(query_idx, result);\n            match best_scores.entry(result.node_id.clone()) {\n                std::collections::hash_map::Entry::Occupied(mut entry) => {\n                    if current_score > *entry.get() {\n                        entry.insert(current_score);\n                    }\n                }\n                std::collections::hash_map::Entry::Vacant(entry) => {\n                    entry.insert(current_score);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Second pass: remove duplicates, keeping only in the query with best score\n    for (query_idx, query_results) in results.iter_mut().enumerate() {\n        query_results.retain(|result| {\n            best_scores\n                .get(&result.node_id)\n                .is_none_or(|best| best.query_idx == query_idx)\n        });\n deprecated_tool_aliases();\n        let tool_names = agent\n            .tools\n            .iter()\n            .flatten()\n            .map(|name| {\n                // Resolve deprecated tool name .filter_map(|pattern| Pattern::new(pattern.as_str()).ok())\n            .collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Matches tool definitions against glob patterns\n    fn match_tools<'a>(&'a self, patterns:  }\n\n    /// Deduplicates tool definitions by name, keeping the first occurrence\n    fn dedupe_tools(&self, resolved: &mut Vec<&ToolDefinition>) {\n        let mut seen = HashSet::new();\n Supports both exact matches\n    /// and glob patterns (e.g., \"fs_*\" matches \"fs_read\", \"fs_write\").\n    /// Filters and deduplicates tool definitions based on agent's tools\n    /// configuration. Returns only the tool definitions that are specified\n    /// in the agent's tools list. Maintains deduplication to avoid\n    /// duplicate tool definitions. Returns tools sorted according to the\n    /// agent's tool order (derived from the tools list).\n    /// Returns references to avoid unnecessary cloning.\n    pub fn resolve<'a>(&'a self, agent: &Agent) -> Vec<&'a ToolDefinition> {\n        let patterns = Self::build_patterns(agent);\n        let mut resolved = self.match_tools(&patterns);\n        self.dedupe_tools(&mut resolved);\n        agent.tool_order().sort_refs(&mut resolved);\n        resolved\n    }\n\n    fn is_allowed_pattern(patterns: &[Pattern], tool_name: &ToolName) -> bool {\n        patterns\n            .iter()\n            .any(|pattern| pattern.matches(tool_name.as_str()))\n    }\n\n    pub fn is_allowed(agent: &Agent, tool_name: &ToolName) -> bool {\n        let aliases = deprecated_tool_aliases();\n        let normalized_tool_name = aliases.get(tool_name.as_str()).unwrap_or(tool_name);\n        let legacy_mcp_tool_name = normalized_tool_name.to_legacy_mcp_name();\n        let patterns = Self::build_patterns(agent);\n\n        Self::is_allowed_pattern(&patterns, normalized_tool_name)\n            || legacy_mcp_tool_name\n                .as_ref()\n                .is_some_and(|legacy_tool_name| {\n                    Self::is_allowed_pattern(&patterns, legacy_tool_name)\n                })\n    }\n\n    /// Builds glob patterns from the agent's tool patterns, deduplicating\n    /// patterns. Supports backward compatibility by automatically adding\n    /// current tool names when deprecated aliases are used.\n    fn build_patterns(agent: &Agent) -> Vec<Pattern> {\n        let aliases = deprecated_tool_aliases();\n        let tool_names = agent\n            .tools\n            .iter()\n            .flatten()\n            .map(|name| {\n                // Resolve deprecated tool name via aliases\n                aliases.get(name.as_str()).unwrap_or(name)\n            })\n            .collect::<HashSet<_>>();\n\n        tool_names\n            .into_iter()\n            .filter_map(|pattern| Pattern::new(pattern.as_str()).ok())\n            .collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Matches tool definitions against glob patterns\n    fn match_tools<'a>(&'a self, patterns: &[Pattern]) -> Vec<&'a ToolDefinition> {\n        self.all_tool_definitions\n            .iter()\n            .filter(|tool| Self::is_allowed_pattern(patterns, &tool.name))\n            .collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Deduplicates tool definitions by name, keeping the first occurrence\n    fn dedupe_tools(&self, resolved: &mut Vec<&ToolDefinition>) {\n        let mut seen = HashSet::new();\n        resolved.retain(|tool| seen.insert(&tool.name));\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use forge_domain::{Agent, AgentId, ModelId, ProviderId, ToolDefinition, ToolName};\n    use This is useful for reducing context size and making\n/// summaries more portable across different environments.\n///\n/// # Platform-Specific Behavior\n///\n/// This implementation uses `std::path::Path::strip_prefix()`, which is\n/// **platform-specific**:\n///\n/// - On **Windows**: Recognizes and strips Windows paths (e.g., `C:\\Users\\...`,\n///   `\\\\server\\share\\...`)\n/// - On **Unix/macOS**: Only recognizes Unix paths (forward slashes). summaries will only be stripped when running on Unix/macOS\n/// - Cross-platform path handling would require a custom implementation that\n///   doesn't rely on the OS-specific `std::path::Path`\n///\n/// For truly cross-platform path stripping (e.g., stripping Windows paths on\n/// Unix or vice versa), consider implementing custom path parsing logic that\n/// handles both std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\n\nuse forge_domain::{ContextSummary, SummaryMessage, SummaryTool, Transformer};\n\n/// Strips the working directory prefix from all file paths in tool calls.\n///\n/// This transformer removes the working directory prefix from file paths in\n/// FileRead, FileUpdate, and FileRemove tool calls, making paths relative to\n/// the working directory. This is useful for reducing context size and making\n/// summaries more portable across different environments.\n///\n/// # Platform-Specific Behavior\n///\n/// This implementation uses `std::path::Path::strip_prefix()`, which is\n/// **platform-specific**:\n///\n/// - On **Windows**: Recognizes and strips Windows paths (e.g., `C:\\Users\\...`,\n///   `\\\\server\\share\\...`)\n/// - On **Unix/macOS**: Only recognizes Unix paths (forward slashes). Windows\n///   paths are treated as literal strings and left unchanged.\n///\n/// This means:\n/// - Windows paths in summaries will only be stripped when running on Windows\n/// - Unix paths in summaries will only be stripped when running on Unix/macOS\n/// - Cross-platform path handling would require a custom implementation that\n///   doesn't rely on the OS-specific `std::path::Path`\n///\n/// For truly cross-platform path stripping (e.g., stripping Windows paths on\n/// Unix or vice versa), consider implementing custom path parsing logic that\n/// handles both path styles regardless of the host OS.\npub struct StripWorkingDir {\n    working_dir: PathBuf,\n}\n\nimpl StripWorkingDir {\n    /// Creates a new StripWorkingDir transformer with the specified working\n    /// directory.\n    ///\n    /// # Arguments\n    ///\n    /// * `working_dir` - The working directory path to strip from file paths\n    pub fn new(working_dir: impl Into<PathBuf>) -> Self {\n        Self { working_dir: working_dir.into() }\n    }\n\n    /// Strips the working directory prefix from a path if present.\n    ///\n    /// Returns the path with the working directory prefix removed, or the\n    /// original path if it doesn't start with the working directory.\n    fn strip_prefix(&self, path: &str) -> String {\n        Path::new(path)\n            .strip_prefix(&self.working_dir)\n            .ok()\n            .and_then(|p| p.to_str())\n            .map(|s| s.to_string())\n            .unwrap_or_else(|| path.to_string())\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Transformer for StripWorkingDir {\n    type Value = ContextSummary;\n\n    fn transform(&mut self, mut summary: Self::Value) -> Self::Value {\n        for message in summary.messages.iter_mut() {\n            for block in message.contents.iter_mut() {\n                if let SummaryMessage::ToolCall(tool_data) = block {\n                    match &mut tool_data.tool {\n                        SummaryTool::FileRead { path } => {\n                            *path = self.strip_prefix(path);\n                        }\n                        SummaryTool::FileUpdate { path } => {\n                            *path = self.strip_prefix(path);\n                        }\n                        SummaryTool::FileRemove { path } => {\n                            *path = self.strip_prefix(path);\n                        }\n                        SummaryTool::Undo { path } => {\n                            *path = self.strip_prefix(path);\n                        }\n                        SummaryTool::Shell { .. }\n                        | SummaryTool::Search { .. }\n                        | SummaryTool::SemSearch { .. }\n                        | SummaryTool::Fetch { .. }\n                        | SummaryTool::Followup { .. }\n                        | SummaryTool::Plan { .. }\n                        | SummaryTool::Skill { .. }\n                        | SummaryTool::Task { .. }\n                        | SummaryTool::Mcp { .. }\n                        | SummaryTool::TodoWrite { .. }\n                        | SummaryTool::TodoRead => {\n                            // These tools don't have paths to strip\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        summary\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use forge_domain::{Role, SummaryBlock, SummaryMessage as Block, SummaryToolCall};\n    use pretty_assertions::assert_eq;\n\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n Logical AND of two policies\n    All { all: Vec<Policy> },\n    /// Logical OR of two policies\n    Any { any: Vec<Policy> },\n    /// Logical NOT of a policy\n    Not { not: Box<Policy> },\n}\n\nimpl Policy {\n    /// Evaluate a policy against an operation\n    pub fn eval(&self, operation: &PermissionOperation) -> Option<Permission> {\n        match self {\n            Policy::Simple { permission, rule } => {\n                let rule_matches = rule.matches(operation);\n                if rule_matches {\n                    Some(permission.clone())\n                } else {\n                    // Rule doesn't match, so this policy doesn't apply\n                    None\n                }\n            }\n            Policy::All { all: and } => {\n                let permissions: Vec<_> = and.iter().map(|policy| policy.eval(operation)).collect();\n                // For AND, we need all policies to pass, return the most restrictive permission\n                permissions\n                    .into_iter()\n                    .find(|permission| permission.is_some())\n                    .flatten()\n            }\n            Policy::Any { any: or } => {\n                let permissions: Vec<_> = or.iter().map(|policy| policy.eval(operation)).collect();\n                // For OR, return the first matching permission\n                permissions\n                    .into_iter()\n                    .find(|permission| permission.is_some())\n                    .flatten()\n            }\n            Policy::Not { not } => {\n                let inner_permission = not.eval(operation);\n                // For NOT, invert the logic - if inner policy denies, we allow, and vice versa\n                match inner_permission {\n                    Some(permission) => {\n                        let inverted_permission = match permission {\n                            Permission::Deny => Permission::Allow,\n                            Permission::Allow => Permission::Deny,\n                            Permission::Confirm => Permission::Deny,\n                        };\n                        Some(inverted_permission)\n                    }\n                    None => None,\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Find all rules that match the given operation\n    pub fn find_rules(&self, operation: &PermissionOperation) -> Vec<&Rule> {\n        let mut rules = Vec::new();\n        self.collect_matching_rules(operation, &mut rules);\n        rules\n    }\n\n    /// Recursively collect all matching rules\n    fn collect_matching_rules<'a>(\n        &'a self,\n        operation: &PermissionOperation,\n        rules: &mut Vec<&'a Rule>,\n    ) {\n        match self {\n            Policy::Simple { permission: _, policy in and {\n                    policy.collect_matching_rules(operation, rules);\n                }\n            }\n            Policy::Any { any: or } => {\n                for policy in or {\n rules);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Get the permission for this policy if it's a simple policy\n    pub fn permission(&self) -> Option<&Permission> {\n        match self {\n JsonSchema)]\n#[serde(untagged)]\n#[serde(rename_all = \"camelCase\")]\npub enum Policy {\n    /// Simple policy with permission and rule\n    Simple { permission: Permission, rule: Rule },\n    /// Logical AND of two policies\n    All { all: Vec<Policy> },\n    /// Logical OR of two policies\n    Any { any: Vec<Policy> },\n    /// Logical NOT of a policy\n    Not { not: Box<Policy> },\n}\n\nimpl Policy {\n    /// Evaluate a policy against an operation\n    pub fn eval(&self, operation: &PermissionOperation) -> Option<Permission> {\n        match self {\n            Policy::Simple { permission, rule } => {\n                let rule_matches = rule.matches(operation);\n                if rule_matches {\n                    Some(permission.clone())\n                } else {\n                    // Rule doesn't match, so this policy doesn't apply\n                    None\n                }\n            }\n            Policy::All { all: and } => {\n                let permissions: Vec<_> = and.iter().map(|policy| policy.eval(operation)).collect();\n                // For AND, we need all policies to pass, return the most restrictive permission\n                permissions\n                    .into_iter()\n                    .find(|permission| permission.is_some())\n                    .flatten()\n            }\n            Policy::Any { any: or } => {\n                let permissions: Vec<_> = or.iter().map(|policy| policy.eval(operation)).collect();\n                // For OR, return the first matching permission\n                permissions\n                    .into_iter()\n                    .find(|permission| permission.is_some())\n                    .flatten()\n            }\n            Policy::Not { not } => {\n                let inner_permission = not.eval(operation);\n                // For NOT, invert the logic - if inner policy denies, we allow, and vice versa\n                match inner_permission {\n                    Some(permission) => {\n                        let inverted_permission = match permission {\n                            Permission::Deny => Permission::Allow,\n                            Permission::Allow => Permission::Deny,\n                            Permission::Confirm => Permission::Deny,\n                        };\n                        Some(inverted_permission)\n                    }\n                    None => None,\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Find all rules that match the given operation\n    pub fn find_rules(&self, operation: &PermissionOperation) -> Vec<&Rule> {\n        let mut rules = Vec::new();\n        self.collect_matching_rules(operation, &mut rules);\n        rules\n    }\n\n    /// Recursively collect all matching rules\n    fn collect_matching_rules<'a>(\n        &'a self,\n        operation: &PermissionOperation,\n        rules: &mut Vec<&'a Rule>,\n    ) {\n        match self {\n            Policy::Simple { permission: _, rule } => {\n                if rule.matches(operation) {\n                    rules.push(rule);\n                }\n            }\n            Policy::All { all: and } => {\n                for policy in and {\n                    policy.collect_matching_rules(operation, rules);\n                }\n            }\n            Policy::Any { any: or } => {\n                for policy in or {\n                    policy.collect_matching_rules(operation, rules);\n                }\n            }\n            Policy::Not { not } => {\n                not.collect_matching_rules(operation, rules);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Get the permission for this policy if it's a simple policy\n    pub fn permission(&self) -> Option<&Permission> {\n        match self {\n            Policy::Simple { permission, rule: _ } => Some(permission),\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Display for Policy {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n let policies: Vec<String> = and.iter().map(|p| p.to_string()).collect();\n                write!(f, \"({})\", policies.join(\" AND \"))\n            }\n            Policy::Any { any: or } => {\n Whether to interrupt the stream when XML\n    ///   tool calls are detected\n    ///\n    /// # Returns\n    /// A ChatCompletionMessageFull containing the aggregated content, tool\n    /// calls, and usage information\n    async fn into_full(\n        self,\n        should_interrupt_for_xml: bool,\n    ) -> Result<ChatCompletionMessageFull, E>;\n\n    /// Collects all messages from the stream into a single\n    /// ChatCompletionMessageFull while streaming content deltas to the sender.\n    ///\n    /// # Arguments\n    /// * `should_interrupt_for_xml` - Whether to interrupt the stream when XML\n    ///   tool calls are detected\n    /// * `sender` - Optional sender to stream content and reasoning deltas to\n    ///\n    /// # Returns\n    /// A ChatCompletionMessageFull containing the aggregated content, tool\n    /// calls, and usage information\n    async fn into_full_streaming(\n        self,\n        should_interrupt_for_xml: bool,\n        sender: Option<ArcSender>,\n    ) -> Result<ChatCompletionMessageFull, E>;\n}\n\n#[async_trait::async_trait]\nimpl ResultStreamExt<anyhow::Error> for crate::BoxStream<ChatCompletionMessage, anyhow::Error> {\n    async fn into_full(\n        self,\n        should_interrupt_for_xml: bool,\n    ) -> anyhow::Result<ChatCompletionMessageFull> {\n        self.into_full_streaming(should_interrupt_for_xml, None)\n            .await\n    }\n\n    async fn into_full_streaming(\n        mut self,\n        should_interrupt_for_xml: bool,\n        sender: Option<ArcSender>,\n    ) -> anyhow::Result<ChatCompletionMessageFull> {\n        let mut messages = Vec::new();\n        let mut usage: Usage = Default::default();\n        let mut content = String::new();\n        let mut xml_tool_calls = None;\n        let mut tool_interrupted = false;\n\n        while let Some(message) = self.next().await {\n            let message =\n                anyhow::Ok(message?).with_context(|| \"Failed to process message stream\")?;\n            // Process usage information\n            // - For Anthropic-style streaming: input tokens in MessageStart, output tokens\n            //   in MessageDelta (values are CUMULATIVE, not incremental)\n            //   ref: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/streaming#event-types\n            // - For example:\n\n  **Good:**\n\n  ```rust,ignore\n  User::default().age(12).is_happy(true).name(\"John\")\n  User::new(\"Job\").age(12).is_happy()\n  User::test() // Special test constructor\n  ```\n\n  **Bad:**\n\n  ```rust,ignore\n  User {name: \"John\".to_string(), is_happy: true, age: 12}\n  User::with_name(\"Job\") // Bad name, should stick to User::new() or User::test()\n  ```\n\n- Use `unwrap()` unless the error information is useful. For example:\n\n  **Good:**\n\n  ```rust,ignore\n  users.first().expect(\"List should not be empty\")\n  ```\n\n  **Bad:**\n\n  ```rust,ignore\n  if let Some(user) = users.first() {\n      // ...\n  } else {\n      panic!(\"List should not be empty\")\n  }\n  ```\n\n- Prefer using `assert_eq` on full objects instead of asserting each field:\n\n  **Good:**\n\n  ```rust,ignore\n  assert_eq!(actual, expected);\n  ```\n\n  **Bad:**\n\n  ```rust,ignore\n  assert_eq!(actual.a, expected.a);\n  assert_eq!(actual.b, expected.b);\n  ```\n\n## Verification\n\nAlways verify changes by running tests and linting the codebase\n\n1. Run crate specific tests to ensure they pass.\n\n   ```\n   cargo insta test --accept\n   ```\n\n2. **Build Guidelines**:\n   - **NEVER** run `cargo build --release` unless absolutely necessary (e.g., performance testing, creating binaries for distribution)\n   - For verification, use `cargo check` (fastest), `cargo insta test`, or `cargo build` (debug mode)\n   - Release builds take significantly longer and are rarely needed for development verification\n\n## Writing Domain Types\n\n- Use `derive_setters` to derive setters and use the `strip_option` and the `into` attributes on the struct types.\n\n## Documentation\n\n- **Always** write Rust docs (`///`) for all public methods, functions, structs, enums, and traits.\n- Document parameters with `# Arguments` and errors with `# Errors` sections when applicable.\n- **Do not include code examples** - docs are for LLMs, not humans. for infrastructure**: Store infrastructure as `Arc&lt;T&gt;` for cheap cloning and shared ownership\n- **Tuple struct pattern**: For simple services with single dependency, use tuple structs `struct Service&lt;T&gt;(Arc&lt;T&gt;)`\n\n### Examples\n\n#### Simple Service (No Infrastructure)\n\n```rust,ignore\npub struct UserValidationService;\n\nimpl UserValidationService {\n    pub fn new() -&gt; Self { ... }\n\n    pub fn validate_email(&amp;self, email: &amp;str) -&gt; Result&lt;()&gt; {\n        // Validation logic here\n        ...\n    }\n\n    pub fn validate_age(&amp;self, age: u32) -&gt; Result&lt;()&gt; {\n        // Age validation logic here\n        ...\n    }\n}\n```\n\n#### Service with Infrastructure Dependency\n\n```rust,ignore\n// Infrastructure trait (defined in infrastructure layer)\npub trait UserRepository {\n    fn find_by_email(&amp;self, email: &amp;str) -&gt; -> Pipe<Self, B> {\n        Pipe(self, other)\n    }\n\n    fn when<F: Fn(&Self::Value) -> bool>(self, cond: F) -> Cond<Self, F>\n    where\n        Self: Sized,\n    {\n        Cond(self, cond)\n    }\n}\n\npub struct DefaultTransformation<T>(PhantomData<T>);\n\nimpl<T> DefaultTransformation<T> {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Self(PhantomData)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<T> Default for Self::Value) -> Self::Value {\n        value\n    }\n}\n\npub struct Cond<A, F>(A, F);\n\nimpl<A, F> Transformer for Cond<A, F>\nwhere\n    A: Transformer,\n    F: Fn(&A::Value) -> bool,\n{\n    type Value = A::Value;\n\n    fn transform(&mut self, value: Self::Value) -> Self::Value {\n        let f = &self.1;\n        if f(&value) {\n            self.0.transform(value)\n        } else {\n            value\n        }\n    }\n}\n\npub struct Pipe<A, B>(A, B);\n\nimpl<A, B, V> Transformer for Pipe<A, B>\nwhere\n    A: Transformer<Value = V>,\n    B: Transformer<Value = V>,\n{\n    type Value =    Error::StartBeyondFileSize { start: start_line, total: total_lines }.into(),\n            );\n        }\n\n        // Cap end position at last line\n        end_pos = cmp::min(end_pos, total_lines total_lines, content_hash);\n\n        // Extract requested lines\n        let result_content = if start_pos == 0 && end_pos == total_lines - 1 {\n            content.to_string() // Return full .unwrap_or_default()\n        };\n\n        Ok((result_content, info))\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod test {\n    use anyhow::Result;\n    use pretty_assertions::assert_eq;\n    use tokio::fs;\n\n styled.push((Style::new(), remaining.to_string()));\n                        break;\n                    }\n                };\n\n                // Look for a `]` that is not immediately after `@[` opener.\n/// - Matches zero or more non-`]` characters inside the brackets.\n/// - Requires closing `]` \342\200\224 unterminated tags are left unstyled.\nfn highlight_mentions(line: &str, styled: &mut StyledText) {\n    let mut remaining = line;\n\n    while !remaining.is_empty() {\n        // Find the next `@[` opener.\n        match remaining.find(\"@[\") {\n            None => {\n  Self {\n            parser: Parser::new(),\n            renderer: Renderer::with_theme(writer, width, theme),\n            line_buffer: String::new(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Push a token to the  Self {\n            parser: Parser::new(),\n            renderer: Renderer::with_theme(writer, width, theme),\n            line_buffer: String::new(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Push a token to the renderer.\n    ///\n    /// Tokens are buffered until a complete line is received, then rendered.\n    pub fn push(&mut self, token: &str) -> io::Result<()> {\n        self.line_buffer.push_str(token);\n\n        while let Some(pos) = self.line_buffer.find('\\n') {\n            let line = self.line_buffer.get(..pos).unwrap_or(\"\").to_string();\n\n            for repaired in repair_line(&line, self.parser.state()) {\n                for event in self.parser.parse_line(&repaired) {\n                    self.renderer.render_event(&event)?;\n                }\n map_reasoning_details_to_input_items(\n    reasoning_details: Vec<ReasoningFull>,\n) -> Vec<oai::InputItem> {\n    // Group all details by ID so we can merge encrypted + summary for each\n    // reasoning item.\n    let mut grouped: HashMap<String, (Option<String>, Vec<String>)> = HashMap::new();\n    // Track insertion order so output is deterministic.\n    let mut order: Vec<String> = Some(\"reasoning.encrypted\") => {\n                if let Some(data) = detail.data\n                    && !data.is_empty()\n                {\n                    entry.0 = Some(data);\n entry.1.push(text);\n                }\n            }\n            _ => {}\n        }\n    }\n\n    order\n        .into_iter()\n        .filter_map(|id| {\n            let (encrypted_content, .collect();\n\n            Some(oai::InputItem::Item(oai::Item::Reasoning(\n                oai::ReasoningItem {\n                    id,\n                    summary,\n                    content: 419279 read(10, "---\nname: create-skill\ndescription: Guide for creating effective skills. This skill should be used when users want to create a new skill (or update an existing skill) that extends your capabilities with specialized knowledge, workflows, or tool integrations.\n---\n\n# Skill Creator\n\nThis skill provides guidance for creating effective skills.\n\n## About Skills\n\nSkills are modular, self-contained packages that extend your capabilities by providing\nspecialized knowledge, workflows, and tools. Think of them as \"onboarding guides\" for specific\ndomains or tasks\342\200\224they transform you from a general-purpose agent into a specialized agent\nequipped with procedural knowledge that no model can fully possess.\n\n### What Skills Provide\n\n1. Specialized workflows - Multi-step procedures for specific domains\n2. Tool integrations - Instructions for working with specific file formats or APIs\n3. Domain expertise - Company-specific knowledge, schemas, business logic\n4. Bundled resources - Scripts, references, and assets for complex and repetitive tasks\n\n## Core Principles\n\n### Concise is Key\n\nThe context window is a public good. Skills share the context window with everything else you need: system prompt, conversation history, other Skills' metadata, and the actual user request.\n\n**Default assumption: You already have significant capabilities.** Only add context you don't already have. Challenge each piece of information: \"Do you really need this explanation?\" and \"Does this paragraph justify its token cost?\"\n\nPrefer concise examples over verbose explanations.\n\n### Set Appropriate Degrees of Freedom\n\nMatch the level of specificity to the task's fragility and variability:\n\n**High freedom (text-based instructions)**: Use when multiple approaches are valid, decisions depend on context, or heuristics guide the approach.\n\n**Medium freedom (pseudocode or scripts with parameters)**: Use when a preferred pattern exists, some variation is acceptable, or configuration affects behavior.\n\n**Low freedom (specific scripts, few parameters)**: Use when operations are fragile and error-prone, consistency is critical, or a specific sequence must be followed.\n\nThink of yourself as exploring a path: a narrow bridge with cliffs needs specific guardrails (low freedom), while an open field allows many routes (high freedom).\n\n### Anatomy of a Skill\n\nEvery skill consists of a required SKILL.md file and optional bundled resources:\n\n```\nskill-name/\n\342\224\234\342\224\200\342\224\200 SKILL.md (required)\n\342\224\202   \342\224\234\342\224\200\342\224\200 YAML frontmatter metadata (required)\n\342\224\202   \342\224\202   \342\224\234\342\224\200\342\224\200 name: (required)\n\342\224\202   \342\224\202   \342\224\224\342\224\200\342\224\200 description: (required)\n\342\224\202   \342\224\224\342\224\200\342\224\200 Markdown instructions (required)\n\342\224\224\342\224\200\342\224\200 Bundled Resources (optional)\n    \342\224\234\342\224\200\342\224\200 scripts/          - Executable code (Python/Bash/etc.)\n    \342\224\234\342\224\200\342\224\200 references/       - Documentation intended to be loaded into context as needed\n    \342\224\224\342\224\200\342\224\200 assets/           - Files used in output (templates, icons, fonts, etc.)\n```\n\n#### SKILL.md (required)\n\nEvery SKILL.md consists of:\n\n- **Frontmatter** (YAML): Contains `name` and `description` fields. These are the only fields you read to determine when the skill gets used, thus it is very important to be clear and comprehensive in describing what the skill is, and when it should be used.\n- **Body** (Markdown): Instructions and guidance for using the skill. Only loaded AFTER the skill triggers (if at all).\n\n#### Bundled Resources (optional)\n\n##### Scripts (`scripts/`)\n\nExecutable code for tasks that require deterministic reliability or are repeatedly rewritten.\n\n- **When to include**: When the same code is being rewritten repeatedly or deterministic reliability is needed\n- **Example**: `scripts/rotate_pdf.sh` for PDF rotation tasks\n- **Benefits**: Token efficient, deterministic, may be executed without loading into context\n- **Note**: Scripts may still need to be read by you for patching or environment-specific adjustments\n\n##### References (`references/`)\n\nDocumentation and reference material intended to be loaded as needed into context to inform your process and thinking.\n\n- **When to include**: For documentation that you should reference while working\n- **Examples**: `references/finance.md` for financial schemas, `references/mnda.md` for company NDA template, `references/policies.md` for company policies, `references/api_docs.md` for API specifications\n- **Use cases**: Database schemas, API documentation, domain knowledge, company policies, detailed workflow guides\n- **Benefits**: Keeps SKILL.md lean, loaded only when you determine it's needed\n- **Best practice**: If files are large (>10k words), include grep search patterns in SKILL.md\n- **Avoid duplication**: Information should live in either SKILL.md or references files, not both. Prefer references files for detailed information unless it's truly core to the skill\342\200\224this keeps SKILL.md lean while making information discoverable without hogging the context window. Keep only essential procedural instructions and workflow guidance in SKILL.md; move detailed reference material, schemas, and examples to references files.\n\n##### Assets (`assets/`)\n\nFiles not intended to be loaded into context, but rather used within the output you produce.\n\n- **When to include**: When the skill needs files that will be used in the final output\n- **Examples**: `assets/logo.png` for brand assets, `assets/slides.pptx` for PowerPoint templates, `assets/frontend-template/` for HTML/React boilerplate, `assets/font.ttf` for typography\n- **Use cases**: Templates, images, icons, boilerplate code, fonts, sample documents that get copied or modified\n- **Benefits**: Separates output resources from documentation, enables you to use files without loading them into context\n\n#### What to Not Include in a Skill\n\nA skill should only contain essential files that directly support its functionality. Do NOT create extraneous documentation or auxiliary files, including:\n\n- README.md\n- INSTALLATION_GUIDE.md\n- QUICK_REFERENCE.md\n- CHANGELOG.md\n- etc.\n\nThe skill should only contain the information needed for an AI agent to do the job at hand. It should not contain auxilary context about the process that went into creating it, setup and testing procedures, user-facing documentation, etc. Creating additional documentation files just adds clutter and confusion.\n\n### Progressive Disclosure Design Principle\n\nSkills use a three-level loading system to manage context efficiently:\n\n1. **Metadata (name + description)** - Always in context (~100 words)\n2. **SKILL.md body** - When skill triggers (<5k words)\n3. **Bundled resources** - As needed by Claude (Unlimited because scripts can be executed without reading into context window)\n\n#### Progressive Disclosure Patterns\n\nKeep SKILL.md body to the essentials and under 500 lines to minimize context bloat. Split content into separate files when approaching this limit. When splitting out content into other files, it is very important to reference them from SKILL.md and describe clearly when to read them, to ensure the reader of the skill knows they exist and when to use them.\n\n**Key principle:** When a skill supports multiple variations, frameworks, or options, keep only the core workflow and selection guidance in SKILL.md. Move variant-specific details (patterns, examples, configuration) into separate reference files.\n\n**Pattern 1: High-level guide with references**\n\n```markdown\n# PDF Processing\n\n## Quick start\n\nExtract text with pdfplumber:\n[code example]\n\n## Advanced features\n\n- **Form filling**: See [FORMS.md](FORMS.md) for complete guide\n- **API reference**: See [REFERENCE.md](REFERENCE.md) for all methods\n- **Examples**: See [EXAMPLES.md](EXAMPLES.md) for common patterns\n```\n\nYou load FORMS.md, REFERENCE.md, or EXAMPLES.md only when needed.\n\n**Pattern 2: Domain-specific organization**\n\nFor Skills with multiple domains, organize content by domain to avoid loading irrelevant context:\n\n```\nbigquery-skill/\n\342\224\234\342\224\200\342\224\200 SKILL.md (overview and navigation)\n\342\224\224\342\224\200\342\224\200 reference/\n    \342\224\234\342\224\200\342\224\200 finance.md (revenue, billing metrics)\n    \342\224\234\342\224\200\342\224\200 sales.md (opportunities, pipeline)\n    \342\224\234\342\224\200\342\224\200 product.md (API usage, features)\n    \342\224\224\342\224\200\342\224\200 marketing.md (campaigns, attribution)\n```\n\nWhen a user asks about sales metrics, you only read sales.md.\n\nSimilarly, for skills supporting multiple frameworks or variants, organize by variant:\n\n```\ncloud-deploy/\n\342\224\234\342\224\200\342\224\200 SKILL.md (workflow + provider selection)\n\342\224\224\342\224\200\342\224\200 references/\n    \342\224\234\342\224\200\342\224\200 aws.md (AWS deployment patterns)\n    \342\224\234\342\224\200\342\224\200 gcp.md (GCP deployment patterns)\n    \342\224\224\342\224\200\342\224\200 azure.md (Azure deployment patterns)\n```\n\nWhen the user chooses AWS, you only read aws.md.\n\n**Pattern 3: Conditional details**\n\nShow basic content, link to advanced content:\n\n```markdown\n# DOCX Processing\n\n## Creating documents\n\nUse docx-js for new documents. See [DOCX-JS.md](DOCX-JS.md).\n\n## Editing documents\n\nFor simple edits, modify the XML directly.\n\n**For tracked changes**: See [REDLINING.md](REDLINING.md)\n**For OOXML details**: See [OOXML.md](OOXML.md)\n```\n\nYou read REDLINING.md or OOXML.md only when the user needs those features.\n\n**Important guidelines:**\n\n- **Avoid deeply nested references** - Keep references one level deep from SKILL.md. All reference files should link directly from SKILL.md.\n- **Structure longer reference files** - For files longer than 100 lines, include a table of contents at the top so you can see the full scope when previewing.\n\n## Skill Creation Process\n\nSkill creation involves these steps:\n\n1. 419279 write(6, "---\nname: create-skill\ndescription: Guide for creating effective skills. This skill should be used when users want to create a new skill (or update an existing skill) that extends your capabilities with specialized knowledge, workflows, or tool integrations.\n---\n\n# Skill Creator\n\nThis skill provides guidance for creating effective skills.\n\n## About Skills\n\nSkills are modular, self-contained packages that extend your capabilities by providing\nspecialized knowledge, workflows, and tools. Think of them as \"onboarding guides\" for specific\ndomains or tasks\342\200\224they transform you from a general-purpose agent into a specialized agent\nequipped with procedural knowledge that no model can fully possess.\n\n### What Skills Provide\n\n1. Specialized workflows - Multi-step procedures for specific domains\n2. Tool integrations - Instructions for working with specific file formats or APIs\n3. Domain expertise - Company-specific knowledge, schemas, business logic\n4. Bundled resources - Scripts, references, and assets for complex and repetitive tasks\n\n## Core Principles\n\n### Concise is Key\n\nThe context window is a public good. Skills share the context window with everything else you need: system prompt, conversation history, other Skills' metadata, and the actual user request.\n\n**Default assumption: You already have significant capabilities.** Only add context you don't already have. Challenge each piece of information: \"Do you really need this explanation?\" and \"Does this paragraph justify its token cost?\"\n\nPrefer concise examples over verbose explanations.\n\n### Set Appropriate Degrees of Freedom\n\nMatch the level of specificity to the task's fragility and variability:\n\n**High freedom (text-based instructions)**: Use when multiple approaches are valid, decisions depend on context, or heuristics guide the approach.\n\n**Medium freedom (pseudocode or scripts with parameters)**: Use when a preferred pattern exists, some variation is acceptable, or configuration affects behavior.\n\n**Low freedom (specific scripts, few parameters)**: Use when operations are fragile and error-prone, consistency is critical, or a specific sequence must be followed.\n\nThink of yourself as exploring a path: a narrow bridge with cliffs needs specific guardrails (low freedom), while an open field allows many routes (high freedom).\n\n### Anatomy of a Skill\n\nEvery skill consists of a required SKILL.md file and optional bundled resources:\n\n```\nskill-name/\n\342\224\234\342\224\200\342\224\200 SKILL.md (required)\n\342\224\202   \342\224\234\342\224\200\342\224\200 YAML frontmatter metadata (required)\n\342\224\202   \342\224\202   \342\224\234\342\224\200\342\224\200 name: (required)\n\342\224\202   \342\224\202   \342\224\224\342\224\200\342\224\200 description: (required)\n\342\224\202   \342\224\224\342\224\200\342\224\200 Markdown instructions (required)\n\342\224\224\342\224\200\342\224\200 Bundled Resources (optional)\n    \342\224\234\342\224\200\342\224\200 scripts/          - Executable code (Python/Bash/etc.)\n    \342\224\234\342\224\200\342\224\200 references/       - Documentation intended to be loaded into context as needed\n    \342\224\224\342\224\200\342\224\200 assets/           - Files used in output (templates, icons, fonts, etc.)\n```\n\n#### SKILL.md (required)\n\nEvery SKILL.md consists of:\n\n- **Frontmatter** (YAML): Contains `name` and `description` fields. These are the only fields you read to determine when the skill gets used, thus it is very important to be clear and comprehensive in describing what the skill is, and when it should be used.\n- **Body** (Markdown): Instructions and guidance for using the skill. Only loaded AFTER the skill triggers (if at all).\n\n#### Bundled Resources (optional)\n\n##### Scripts (`scripts/`)\n\nExecutable code for tasks that require deterministic reliability or are repeatedly rewritten.\n\n- **When to include**: When the same code is being rewritten repeatedly or deterministic reliability is needed\n- **Example**: `scripts/rotate_pdf.sh` for PDF rotation tasks\n- **Benefits**: Token efficient, deterministic, may be executed without loading into context\n- **Note**: Scripts may still need to be read by you for patching or environment-specific adjustments\n\n##### References (`references/`)\n\nDocumentation and reference material intended to be loaded as needed into context to inform your process and thinking.\n\n- **When to include**: For documentation that you should reference while working\n- **Examples**: `references/finance.md` for financial schemas, `references/mnda.md` for company NDA template, `references/policies.md` for company policies, `references/api_docs.md` for API specifications\n- **Use cases**: Database schemas, API documentation, domain knowledge, company policies, detailed workflow guides\n- **Benefits**: Keeps SKILL.md lean, loaded only when you determine it's needed\n- **Best practice**: If files are large (>10k words), include grep search patterns in SKILL.md\n- **Avoid duplication**: Information should live in either SKILL.md or references files, not both. Prefer references files for detailed information unless it's truly core to the skill\342\200\224this keeps SKILL.md lean while making information discoverable without hogging the context window. Keep only essential procedural instructions and workflow guidance in SKILL.md; move detailed reference material, schemas, and examples to references files.\n\n##### Assets (`assets/`)\n\nFiles not intended to be loaded into context, but rather used within the output you produce.\n\n- **When to include**: When the skill needs files that will be used in the final output\n- **Examples**: `assets/logo.png` for brand assets, `assets/slides.pptx` for PowerPoint templates, `assets/frontend-template/` for HTML/React boilerplate, `assets/font.ttf` for typography\n- **Use cases**: Templates, images, icons, boilerplate code, fonts, sample documents that get copied or modified\n- **Benefits**: Separates output resources from documentation, enables you to use files without loading them into context\n\n#### What to Not Include in a Skill\n\nA skill should only contain essential files that directly support its functionality. Do NOT create extraneous documentation or auxiliary files, including:\n\n- README.md\n- INSTALLATION_GUIDE.md\n- QUICK_REFERENCE.md\n- CHANGELOG.md\n- etc.\n\nThe skill should only contain the information needed for an AI agent to do the job at hand. Split content into separate files when approaching this limit. When splitting out content into other files, it is very important to reference them from SKILL.md and describe clearly when to read them, to ensure the reader of the skill knows they exist and when to use them.\n\n**Key principle:** When a skill supports multiple variations, frameworks, or options, keep only the core workflow and selection guidance in SKILL.md. If the input cannot be converted to yes/no, the prompt is\n    /// repeated in a loop until a valid response or cancellation is received.\n    ///\n    /// # Returns\n    ///\n    /// - `Ok(Some(true))` - User confirmed (Y, y, yes, YES, etc.)\n    /// - `Ok(Some(false))` - User denied (N, n, no, NO, etc.)\n    /// - `Ok(None)` - User cancelled (EOF / Ctrl+D / Ctrl+C)\n    /// - `Err(...)` - If the prompt fails\n    pub fn prompt(self) -> Result<Option<bool>> {\n        let hint = match self.default {\n            Some(true) => \"Y/n\".to_string(),\n            Some(false) => \"y/N\".to_string(),\n            None => \"y/n\".to_string(),\n        };\n\n        let message_with_hint = if cfg!(windows) {\n            format!(\"{} {}\", self.message, hint)\n        } else {\n            format!(\"{} {}\", self.message, hint.yellow())\n        };\n\n        loop {\n            let input_builder = InputBuilder {\n                message: message_with_hint.clone(),\n                allow_empty: true,\n                default: None,\n                default_display: None,\n            };\n\n            let result = input_builder.prompt()?;\n\n            // User cancelled (Ctrl+C or EOF)\n            if result.is_none() {\n                return Ok(None);\n            }\n\n            let input = result.unwrap().trim().to_lowercase();\n\n            // Empty input - use default\n            if input.is_empty() {\n                return Ok(Some(self.default.unwrap_or(false)));\n            }\n\n            // Parse Y/N response\n            if input == \"y\" || input == \"yes\" {\n                return Ok(Some(true));\n            }\n            if input == \"n\" || input == \"no\" {\n                return Ok(Some(false));\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n", 2437) = 2437

Clone, PartialEq)]\npub struct ClipperResult<'a> {\n    /// The actual content passed for truncation.\n    pub actual: &'a str,\n    /// The prefix portion of the truncated content (if applicable)\n    pub prefix: Option<Range<usize>>,\n    /// The suffix portion of the truncated content (if applicable)\n    pub suffix: Option<Range<usize>>,\n}\n\nimpl ClipperResult<'_> {\n    /// Check if this exists\n    pub fn suffix_content(&self) -> Option<&str> {\n        self.suffix\n            .as_ref()\n            .and_then(|range| self.actual.get(range.clone()))\n    }\n}\n\n/// A strategy for PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum Clipper {\n    /// Retains data from the beginning up to the specified character count\n    Prefix(usize),\n\n    /// Retains data from both the beginning and end of the content\n    /// First parameter is the prefix character count\n    /// Second parameter is the suffix character count\n    PrefixSuffix(usize, usize),\n\n    /// Retains data from the end up to the specified character count\n    Suffix(usize),\n}\n\nimpl Default for Clipper {\n    /// Creates a default Clipper that keeps the prefix up to MAX_LIMIT\n    /// characters\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::Prefix(MAX_LIMIT)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Clipper {\n    /// Creates a Clipper that keeps the prefix (beginning) of the content\n    /// up to the specified number of characters\n    pub fn characters\n    pub fn from_end(suffix_chars: usize) -> Clipper {\n        Self::Suffix(suffix_chars)\n    }\n\n    /// Creates a Clipper that keeps both the beginning and end of the content\n    /// Normalise incoming values\n    let s0 = start_line.unwrap_or(1).max(1);\n    let e0 = end_line.unwrap_or(s0.saturating_add(max_size.saturating_sub(1)));\n\n    // 2. Sort them (min \342\206\222 start, max \342\206\222 end) and force start \342\211\245 1\n    let start = s0.min(e0).max(1);\n    let mut end = s0.max(e0);\n\n    // 3. Clamp the range length to `max_size`\n    end = end.min(start.saturating_add(max_size.saturating_sub(1)));\n\n    (start, end)\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use 419279 read(10, "# Claude Tool Description Best Practices\n\n## Key Principles\n\nWhen defining tools for Claude to use, the quality of your tool descriptions dramatically affects performance. Here are the most important best practices extracted from Anthropic's documentation:\n\n### 1. Provide Extremely Detailed Descriptions\n\nThis is by far the most important factor in tool performance. Your descriptions should explain every detail about the tool, including:\n\n- **What the tool does** - Be explicit about the tool's primary function and purpose\n- **When it should be used** - Specify the scenarios where this tool is appropriate\n- **When it should NOT be used** - Clarify scenarios where the tool is not suitable\n- **What each parameter means** - Explain how each parameter affects the tool's behavior\n- **Limitations and caveats** - Note what information the tool does not return or handle\n- **Additional context** - If the tool name is unclear, provide extra clarification\n\n### 2. Use Comprehensive But Concise Descriptions\n\nThe more context you can give Claude about your tools, the better it will be at deciding when and how to use them. Aim for 3-4 sentences per tool description, or more if the tool is complex.\n\n> **IMPORTANT**: Tool descriptions must never exceed 1024 characters. This is enforced by tests to ensure compatibility with LLM API constraints.\n\n### 3. Prioritize Descriptions Over Examples\n\nWhile you can include examples of how to use a tool in its description or in the accompanying prompt, this is less important than having a clear and comprehensive explanation of the tool's purpose and parameters. Only add examples after you've fully fleshed out the description.\n\n### 4. Register All Tools in the Registry\n\nEvery tool must be registered in the `crates/forge_services/src/tools/registry.rs` file to be available for use. 419279 read(10, "# Dynamic System Context Rendering with Variables\n\n## Objective\n\nModify the system context rendering mechanism to:\n\n\n1. Re-render the system context on every conversation turn\n2. Pass variables to the system context renderer (similar to event rendering)\n\nThe current implementation renders the system context only once during agent initialization, which means time-sensitive information like `current_time` is not updated. Additionally, the system context cannot use dynamic variables from the conversation state.\n\n## Implementation Plan\n\n### 1. Update TemplateService Trait\n\nModify the `TemplateService` trait in `crates/forge_domain/src/services.rs` to include variables in the `render_system` method signature:\n\n```rust\nasync fn render_system(\n    &self,\n    agent: &Agent,\n    prompt: &Template<SystemContext>,\n    variables: &HashMap<String, Value>,\n) -> anyhow::Result<String>;\n```\n\n### 2. Modify ForgeTemplateService Implementation\n\nUpdate the implementation in `crates/forge_services/src/template.rs` to handle variables in system context rendering:\n\n```rust\nasync fn render_system(\n    &self,\n    _agent: &Agent,\n    prompt: &Template<SystemContext>,\n    variables: &HashMap<String, Value>,\n) -> anyhow::Result<String> {\n    let env = self.infra.environment_service().get_environment();\n\n    // Build the walker, only setting max_depth if a value was provided\n    let mut walker = Walker::max_all();\n\n    // Only set max_depth if the value is provided\n    // Create maximum depth for file walker, defaulting to 1 if not specified\n    walker = walker.max_depth(_agent.max_walker_depth.unwrap_or(1));\n\n    let mut files = walker\n        .cwd(env.cwd.clone())\n        .get()\n        .await?\n        .iter()\n        .map(|f| f.path.to_string())\n        .collect::<Vec<_>>();\n\n    // Sort the files alphabetically to ensure consistent ordering\n    files.sort();\n\n    // Get current date and time with timezone\n    let current_time = Local::now().format(\"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %:z\").to_string();\n\n    // Create the context with README content for all agents\n    let ctx = SystemContext {\n        current_time,\n        env: Some(env),\n        tool_information: Some(self.tool_service.usage_prompt()),\n        tool_supported: _agent.tool_supported.unwrap_or_default(),\n        files,\n        readme: README_CONTENT.to_string(),\n        custom_rules: _agent.custom_rules.as_ref().cloned().unwrap_or_default(),\n        variables: variables.clone(), // Add the variables\n    };\n\n    // Render the template with the context\n    let result = self.hb.render_template(prompt.template.as_str(), &ctx)?;\n    Ok(result)\n}\n```\n\n### 3. Update SystemContext Struct\n\nModify the `SystemContext` struct in `crates/forge_domain/src/system_context.rs` to include variables:\n\n```rust\n#[derive(Debug, Setters, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n#[setters(strip_option)]\npub struct SystemContext {\n    // Current date and time at the time of context creation\n    pub current_time: String,\n    \n    // Environment information to be included in the system context\n    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n    pub env: Option<Environment>,\n\n    // Information about available tools that can be used by the agent\n    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n    pub tool_information: Option<String>,\n\n    /// Indicates whether the agent supports tools.\n    /// This value is populated directly from the Agent configuration.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub tool_supported: bool,\n\n    // List of file paths that are relevant for the agent context\n    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = \"Vec::is_empty\")]\n    pub files: Vec<String>,\n\n    // README content to provide project context to the agent\n    pub readme: String,\n\n    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = \"String::is_empty\")]\n    pub custom_rules: String,\n    \n    // Variables to pass to the system context\n    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = \"HashMap::is_empty\")]\n    pub variables: HashMap<String, Value>,\n}\n\n// Update the Default implementation if it exists\nimpl Default for SystemContext {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            current_time: String::new(),\n            env: None,\n            tool_information: None,\n            tool_supported: false,\n            files: Vec::new(),\n            readme: String::new(),\n            custom_rules: String::new(),\n            variables: HashMap::new(),\n        }\n    }\n}\n```\n\n### 4. Update Orchestrator to Re-render System Context\n\nModify the orchestrator's conversation loop in `crates/forge_domain/src/orch.rs` to re-render the system context on each iteration:\n\n```rust\nasync fn init_agent(&self, agent_id: &AgentId, event: &Event) -> anyhow::Result<()> {\n    let conversation = self.get_conversation().await?;\n    debug!(\n        conversation_id = %conversation.id,\n        agent = %agent_id,\n        event = ?event,\n        \"Initializing agent\"\n    );\n    let agent = conversation.workflow.get_agent(agent_id)?;\n\n    let mut context = if agent.ephemeral.unwrap_or_default() {\n        self.init_agent_context(agent).await?\n    } else {\n        match conversation.context(&agent.id) {\n            Some(context) => context.clone(),\n            None => self.init_agent_context(agent).await?,\n        }\n    };\n\n    if let Some(temperature) = agent.temperature {\n        context = context.temperature(temperature);\n    }\n\n    let content = if let Some(user_prompt) = &agent.user_prompt {\n        // Get conversation variables from the conversation\n        let variables = &conversation.variables;\n\n        // Use the consolidated render_event method which handles suggestions and\n        // variables\n        self.services\n            .template_service()\n            .render_event(agent, user_prompt, event, variables)\n            .await?\n    } else {\n        // Use the raw event value as content if no user_prompt is provided\n        event.value.to_string()\n    };\n\n    if !content.is_empty() {\n        context = context.add_message(ContextMessage::user(content));\n    }\n\n    // Process attachments\n    let attachments = self\n        .services\n        .attachment_service()\n        .attachments(&event.value.to_string())\n        .await?;\n\n    for attachment in attachments.into_iter() {\n        match attachment.content_type {\n            ContentType::Image => {\n                context = context.add_message(ContextMessage::Image(attachment.content));\n            }\n            ContentType::Text => {\n                let content = format!(\n
