419279 write(6, "# Dynamic System Context Rendering with Variables\n\n## Objective\n\nModify the system context rendering mechanism to:\n\n\n1. Re-render the system context on every conversation turn\n2. Pass variables to the system context renderer (similar to event rendering)\n\nThe current implementation renders the system context only once during agent initialization, which means time-sensitive information like `current_time` is not updated. Additionally, the system context cannot use dynamic variables from the conversation state.\n\n## Implementation Plan\n\n### 1. Update TemplateService Trait\n\nModify the `TemplateService` trait in `crates/forge_domain/src/services.rs` to include variables in the `render_system` method signature:\n\n```rust\nasync fn render_system(\n    &self,\n    agent: &Agent,\n    prompt: &Template<SystemContext>,\n    variables: &HashMap<String, Value>,\n) -> anyhow::Result<String>;\n```\n\n### 2. Modify ForgeTemplateService Implementation\n\nUpdate the implementation in `crates/forge_services/src/template.rs` to handle variables in system context rendering:\n\n```rust\nasync fn render_system(\n    &self,\n    _agent: &Agent,\n    prompt: &Template<SystemContext>,\n    variables: &HashMap<String, Value>,\n) -> anyhow::Result<String> {\n    let env = self.infra.environment_service().get_environment();\n\n    // Build the walker, only setting max_depth if a value was provided\n    let mut walker = Walker::max_all();\n\n    // Only set max_depth if the value is provided\n    // Create maximum depth for file walker, defaulting to 1 if not specified\n    walker = walker.max_depth(_agent.max_walker_depth.unwrap_or(1));\n\n    let mut files = walker\n        .cwd(env.cwd.clone())\n        .get()\n        .await?\n        .iter()\n        .map(|f| f.path.to_string())\n        .collect::<Vec<_>>();\n\n    // Sort the files alphabetically to ensure consistent ordering\n    files.sort();\n\n    // Get current date and time with timezone\n    let current_time = Local::now().format(\"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %:z\").to_string();\n\n    // Create the context with README content for all agents\n    let ctx = SystemContext {\n        current_time,\n        env: Some(env),\n        tool_information: Some(self.tool_service.usage_prompt()),\n        tool_supported: _agent.tool_supported.unwrap_or_default(),\n        files,\n        readme: README_CONTENT.to_string(),\n        custom_rules: _agent.custom_rules.as_ref().cloned().unwrap_or_default(),\n        variables: variables.clone(), // Add the variables\n    };\n\n    // Render the template with the context\n    let result = self.hb.render_template(prompt.template.as_str(), &ctx)?;\n    Ok(result)\n}\n```\n\n### 3. Update SystemContext Struct\n\nModify the `SystemContext` struct in `crates/forge_domain/src/system_context.rs` to include variables:\n\n```rust\n#[derive(Debug, Setters, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n#[setters(strip_option)]\npub struct SystemContext {\n    // Current date and time at the time of context creation\n    pub current_time: String,\n    \n    // Environment information to be included in the system context\n    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n    pub env: Option<Environment>,\n\n    // Information about available tools that can be used by the agent\n    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n    pub tool_information: Option<String>,\n\n    /// Indicates whether the agent supports tools.\n    /// This value is populated directly from the Agent configuration.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub tool_supported: bool,\n\n    // List of file paths that are relevant for the agent context\n    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = \"Vec::is_empty\")]\n    pub files: Vec<String>,\n\n    // README content to provide project context to the agent\n    pub readme: String,\n\n    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = \"String::is_empty\")]\n    pub custom_rules: String,\n    \n    // Variables to pass to the system context\n    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = \"HashMap::is_empty\")]\n    pub variables: HashMap<String, Value>,\n}\n\n// Update the Default implementation if it exists\nimpl Default for SystemContext {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            current_time: String::new(),\n            env: None,\n            tool_information: None,\n            tool_supported: false,\n            files: Vec::new(),\n            readme: String::new(),\n            custom_rules: String::new(),\n            variables: HashMap::new(),\n        }\n    }\n}\n```\n\n### 4. 419279 read(10, "# Config Read at Application Init \342\200\224 Surface Errors, Remove Silent Defaults\n\n## Objective\n\nCurrently, `ForgeConfig` is read lazily from disk inside `ForgeEnvironmentInfra` and any parse/deserialization errors are silently swallowed \342\200\224 returning `ForgeConfig::default()` (all-zero values) with only a tracing log that the user never sees. This causes silent breakage of all tool limits and agent parameters when the user's config file is corrupt or invalid.\n\nThe goal is to:\n1. Read `ForgeConfig` **once at application startup** in `main.rs`, surfacing any parse error directly to the user before the app proceeds.\n2. Pass the pre-read config through the construction chain to every consumer.\n3. **Remove `get_config()` from the `EnvironmentInfra` trait** entirely \342\200\224 it is no longer needed since config is injected at construction time.\n4. Preserve the `update_environment` write path so that `forge config set` commands continue to work correctly.\n\n---\n\n## Architecture Overview\n\n### Current Flow (Lazy, Silent-Error)\n\n```\nmain.rs\n  \342\224\224\342\224\200 ForgeAPI::init(cwd)\n       \342\224\224\342\224\200 ForgeInfra::new(cwd)\n            \342\224\224\342\224\200 ForgeEnvironmentInfra::new(cwd)      \342\206\220 cache = None\n                 \342\224\224\342\224\200 (first get_config() call)\n                      \342\224\224\342\224\200 ForgeConfig::read()         \342\206\220 disk I/O\n                           \342\224\224\342\224\200 Err(_) \342\206\222 Default::default()  \342\206\220 SILENT!\n```\n\n### Target Flow (Eager, Error-Surfaced)\n\n```\nmain.rs\n  \342\224\224\342\224\200 ForgeConfig::read()?                            \342\206\220 fails loudly here\n  \342\224\224\342\224\200 ForgeAPI::init(cwd, config)\n       \342\224\224\342\224\200 ForgeInfra::new(cwd, config)\n            \342\224\224\342\224\200 ForgeEnvironmentInfra::new(cwd, config)  \342\206\220 cache = Some(config)\n            \342\224\224\342\224\200 ForgeHttpInfra::new(config, ...)\n            \342\224\224\342\224\200 ForgeDirectoryReaderService::new(config.max_parallel_file_reads)\n            \342\224\224\342\224\200 ForgeGrpcClient::new(config.services_url.parse()?)\n```\n\n### What `update_environment` Does (Preserved)\n\n`ForgeEnvironmentInfra::update_environment` performs a **read-from-disk \342\206\222 mutate \342\206\222 write-to-disk \342\206\222 cache-invalidate** cycle whenever the user changes provider/model/reasoning settings. After invalidation, the next `get_config()` call re-reads from disk. Since `get_config()` is being removed from the trait, the internal cache mechanism in `ForgeEnvironmentInfra` must be adapted so the fresh post-write value is propagated back to all consumers that hold a stored config.\n\nThe cleanest resolution: `update_environment` returns the updated `ForgeConfig` in its result, and callers store the new value. However, since the trait is used in many places, the simplest compatible approach is to keep the cache internal to `ForgeEnvironmentInfra` but make `update_environment` callable from the services layer to update its stored config \342\200\224 or to have the application re-read config after an update via a narrower dedicated trait method (not `get_config()` on the general infra trait).\n\n---\n\n## Key Invariants to Preserve\n\n1. **`update_environment` must still work** \342\200\224 `forge config set model ...` must update the TOML and the in-memory state visible to subsequent calls.\n2. **`/new` conversation re-creation** \342\200\224 `on_new()` calls `(self.new_api)()`, rebuilding `ForgeAPI`. The captured `ForgeConfig` in the closure must be the **latest** config (post any `update_environment` calls), not the startup snapshot.\n3. **`get_config()` removal scope** \342\200\224 removing it from `EnvironmentInfra` does not mean removing it from every consumer; it means the consumers receive the value as a constructor argument or method parameter rather than calling `infra.get_config()` at runtime.\n4. **`services_url` panic elimination** \342\200\224 with config surfaced in `main.rs`, the `.expect()` on `services_url.parse()` can be converted to `?`-propagation, making `ForgeInfra::new()` fallible.\n\n---\n\n## Implementation Plan\n\n### Phase 1 \342\200\224 Surface Config Errors in `ForgeConfig::read()`\n\n- [~] Task 1.1. **Fix silent error in `ConfigReader::read_global()`** (`crates/forge_config/src/reader.rs`): The `.required(false)` flag on `config::File::from(path)` silently swallows parse errors for malformed TOML files. Change this so that if the file *exists* but is invalid (e.g., malformed TOML, wrong types), an error is returned. Only missing files should be silently skipped. This may require checking file existence before adding the `config` source, or using a custom file reader that returns `Err` on parse failure but `Ok` on file-not-found.\n\n- [ ] Task 1.2. **Fix silent skip in `ConfigReader::read_legacy()`** (`crates/forge_config/src/reader.rs`): Currently uses `if let Ok(content) = content { ... } else { self }` \342\200\224 silently ignores errors. Change to at minimum emit a `warn!` log message, or propagate the error. Since legacy JSON is a migration concern, a `warn!` is appropriate rather than a hard error.\n\n- [ ] Task 1.3. **Verify `ForgeConfig::read()` return type** \342\200\224 it already returns `anyhow::Result<ForgeConfig>`. No signature change needed here. The fix is upstream in the reader chain ensuring errors actually reach the `Result::Err` variant.\n\n### Phase 2 \342\200\224 Read Config Once in `main.rs`\n\n- [ ] Task 2.1. **Call `ForgeConfig::read()` at the top of `main()` in `crates/forge_main/src/main.rs`** before the `UI::init` call. The error message from `anyhow` will include the cause (e.g., \"invalid TOML at line 12: expected string, found integer\"), which is exactly what the user needs to see.\n\n- [ ] Task 2.2. **Thread the `config: ForgeConfig` into the `UI::init` factory closure** in `main.rs`. `decl-splitter`, `decl-lattice`, `decl-patterns`). It will reuse all existing syn-based visitors and fingerprint structures.\n\nThe pipeline has three stages that feed into each other: split and fingerprint source files into declarative fingerprints, group those fingerprints into a similarity lattice based on equivalence classes, and build a term reverse index from all identifiers across all declarations. Stage 1 reuses the existing `decl-splitter` split logic and adds fingerprint computation. Stage 2 groups fingerprints into equivalence classes (isomorphic functions) and builds a lattice layer from those groups. Stage 3 walks all declarations and builds an inverted index mapping every identifier/term to the list of declarations that reference it.\n\n### Files to Create\n\n- [ ] Create `src/term_index.rs` \342\200\224 New module in the `decl_splitter` workspace containing the term reverse index logic. Defines a `TermIndex` struct that maps normalized terms (identifiers, type names, crate names, method names, qualifier keywords) to `Vec<DeclLocation>` entries. Each `DeclLocation` stores the file path, declaration name, kind, project name, and fingerprint hash. The module exposes the `build_term_index` function which takes a directory of split decl files and returns the populated `TermIndex`. Uses the existing `IdentCollector` and `UseCrateCollector` AST visitors from `src/lattice.rs` to extract terms from each declaration. Normalizes terms by lowercasing and stripping common suffixes/prefixes. Deduplicates within each document so a term appears once per decl.\n\n- [ ] Create `src/merge_index.rs` \342\200\224 New module containing the similarity-based lattice merge logic. Defines a `SimilarityLattice` struct where each node is a `FunctionEquivalenceClass`: a group of declarations sharing the same `DeclFingerprint` (from `src/fingerprint.rs`). The `structural_shape` hash serves as the primary equivalence key; declarations with identical shape + same `crates_used` set are grouped together. The module exposes the `build_similarity_lattice` function which: (a) loads all fingerprint JSON files, (b) groups by structural_shape and crates_used tuple, (c) discards singletons (unique functions), (d) sorts equivalence classes by size descending, (e) assigns each class to a lattice layer based on topological depth of its declaration dependencies, (f) serializes the lattice to `similarity_lattice.json`. Uses the existing `decl-lattice` layering logic from `src/lattice.rs:381-415`.\n\n- [ ] Create `src/bin/term-index.rs` \342\200\224 New CLI binary entry point. Accepts arguments: `--decls-dir` (directory of split decl files), `--fingerprints-dir` (directory with fingerprint JSON files), `--output` (output directory). Orchestrates the three-stage pipeline: runs `build_term_index`, writes `term_index.json`; runs `build_similarity_lattice`, writes `similarity_lattice.json`. Reports summary statistics: total declarations, unique terms, equivalence classes, largest equivalence class, terms per document average.\n\n- [ ] Update `Cargo.toml` \342\200\224 Register the new `[[bin]]` entry for `term-index` at `src/bin/term-index.rs`. Each key in the index map is a normalized term string (lowercased identifier). The value for each term is an array of declaration location objects, each containing the file path, declaration name, declaration kind, and project name. The stats section records total declarations indexed, unique terms discovered, and distribution metrics like max and median documents per term.\n\n### SimilarityLattice Output (`similarity_lattice.json`)\n\nThe similarity lattice is a JSON object with three sections: an `equivalence_classes` array, a `layers` array, and a `stats` section. Each equivalence class has a unique identifier, the shape hash that defines the equivalence, an array of member declarations (file path, declaration name, project name), a lattice layer assignment, and an isomorphism flag. The layers section maps lattice depth to the list of equivalence class identifiers at that depth. The stats section reports total declarations processed, number of equivalence classes found, number of singletons discarded, and the size of the largest class.\n\n## Verification Criteria\n\n- [ ] `cargo build --bin term-index` compiles cleanly with no errors\n- [ ] Running `term-index --decls-dir /tmp/decls_forge_domain --fingerprints-dir /tmp/fingerprints --output /tmp/term-index-output` produces valid `term_index.json` with at least 100 unique terms\n- [ ] verified: the index has string keys, each mapping to an array of objects with file, decl, kind, and project fields\n- [ ] `similarity_lattice.json` contains at least 1 equivalence class with 2+ members (isomorphic functions across projects)\n- [ ] Running the tool on all available decl archives (forge_domain, pi_agent, cargo-vendormod's 508 decls) produces index entries for every declaration\n- [ ] No regressions in existing binaries (`decl-splitter`, `decl-lattice`, `decl-patterns`) \342\200\224 all still compile and pass existing tests\n\n## Potential Risks and Mitigations\n\n1. **Fingerprint hash collisions**: Two structurally different declarations could produce the same `structural_shape` hash. Mitigation: use the full DeclFingerprint tuple of kind, crates_used, shape_hash, trait_bounds, visibility, and qualifiers as the equivalence key, not just the hash alone. The hash is a 64-bit value from `std::hash::DefaultHasher` which has a 2^-64 collision probability per pair \342\200\224 negligible at this scale.\n\n2. **Index size blowup**: A large codebase (arti-tor-rs has 7,335 decls) could produce a term index with millions of entries. Mitigation: deduplicate terms per document (one entry per term per decl), use compact JSON encoding, and consider streaming serialization for very large outputs. The existing decl archives from cargo-vendormod (947,362 files) already demonstrate the system handles this scale.\n\n3. **Equivalence class sparsity**: Most functions might be unique (singletons), producing few meaningful equivalence classes. Mitigation: the pipeline discards singletons by design and only reports groups of 2+. If the ratio is too low, the fingerprint granularity can be reduced (e.g., ignore `visibility_class` or `qualifiers` for a looser grouping). The existing pattern matcher at `patterns.rs:340-346` already implements overlap scoring that can be used for fuzzy matching if exact matches are insufficient.\n\n## Alternative Approaches\n\n1. **Fuzzy fingerprint matching**: Instead of exact `(shape_hash, crates_used)` equivalence, use Jaccard similarity on crate usage sets to find near-isomorphic functions. Trade-off: catches more matches but introduces a threshold parameter. The existing `overlap_score` function at `patterns.rs:452-461` provides a foundation for this.\n\n2. **Full-text search index**: Instead of an AST-level term index, use a simple `rg`/grep-based inverted index built from raw source text. Trade-off: faster to build but misses type-aware information (e.g., cannot distinguish `use serde::Serialize` from a variable named `serde`). The AST-based approach is more precise.\n\n3. **Database-backed index**: Instead of JSON files, use SQLite for the term index and equivalence lattice. Trade-off: enables efficient queries (WHERE term = 'serde' AND project = 'forge_domain') but adds a build dependency. JSON is simpler for initial implementation and sufficient for the target scale (< 100K decls).\n", 9892) = 9892

It then builds a new compacted context with just the summary\n\nThis approach doesn't distinguish between different message roles or sequences, treating all messages equally in the compaction process.\n\n## Implementation Plan\n\n### 1. Identify Compressible Sequences\n\nAdd functionality to identify sequences of assistant messages that qualify for compression:\n\n```rust\n/// Identifies sequences of assistant messages that can be compressed (2+ consecutive messages)\nfn identify_compressible_sequences(&self, context: &Context) -> Vec<(usize, usize)> {\n    let messages = context.messages();\n    let mut sequences = Vec::new();\n    let mut current_sequence_start: Option<usize> = None;\n    \n    for (i, message) in messages.iter().enumerate() {\n        if message.is_assistant() {\n            // Start a new sequence or continue current one\n            if current_sequence_start.is_none() {\n                current_sequence_start = Some(i);\n            }\n        } else {\n            // End of a potential sequence\n            if let Some(start) = current_sequence_start {\n                // Only compress sequences with more than 1 assistant message\n                if i - start > 1 {\n                    sequences.push((start, i - 1));\n                }\n                current_sequence_start = None;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    \n    // Check for a sequence at the end\n    if let Some(start) = current_sequence_start {\n        let end = messages.len() - 1;\n        if end - start > 0 {  // More than 1 message\n            sequences.push((start, end));\n        }\n    }\n    \n    sequences\n}\n```\n\n### 2. original_context: Context, \n    sequences: Vec<(usize, usize)>\n) -> Result<Context> {\n    let messages = original_context.messages();\n    let mut compacted_messages = Vec::new();\n    \n    let mut next_index = 0;\n    \n    // Process each sequence\n    for (start, end) in sequences {\n        // Add any messages before this sequence\n        compacted_messages.extend(messages[next_index..start].to_vec());\n        \n        // Extract the sequence to summarize\n        let sequence = &messages[start..=end];\n        \n        // Only compacted_messages.extend(sequence.to_vec());\n        }\n        \n        next_index = end + 1;\n    }\n    \n    // Add any remaining messages\n    if next_index < messages.len() {\n        compacted_messages.extend(messages[next_index..].to_vec());\n    }\n    \n    // Build the new context\n    let mut compacted_context = Context::default();\n    \n    // Add system message if present 419279 read(10, "# Forge ZSH Plugin\n\nA powerful ZSH plugin that provides intelligent command transformation, file tagging, and conversation management for the Forge AI assistant.\n\n## Features\n\n- **Smart Command Transformation**: Convert `:command` syntax into forge executions\n- **Agent Selection**: Tab completion for available agents using `:agent_name`\n- **File Tagging**: Interactive file selection with `@[filename]` syntax\n- **Syntax Highlighting**: Visual feedback for commands and tagged files\n- **Conversation Continuity**: Automatic session management across commands\n- **Interactive Completion**: Fuzzy finding for files and agents via built-in picker\n\n## Prerequisites\n\nBefore using this plugin, ensure you have the following tools installed:\n\n- **fd** - Fast file finder (alternative to find)\n- **forge** - The Forge CLI tool\n\n### Installation of Prerequisites\n\n```bash\n# macOS (using Homebrew)\nbrew install fd\n\n# Ubuntu/Debian\nsudo apt install fd-find\n\n# Arch Linux\nsudo pacman -S fd\n```\n\n## Usage\n\n### Starting a Conversation\n\nBegin any command with `:` followed by your prompt:\n\n```bash\n: Get the current time\n```\n\nThis automatically starts a new conversation with the default Forge agent.\n\n### Using Specific Agents\n\nSpecify an agent by name after the colon:\n\n```bash\n:sage How does caching work in this system?\n:muse Create a deployment strategy for my app\n```\n\n**Tab Completion**: Type `:` followed by partial agent name and press `TAB` for interactive selection.\n\n### File Tagging\n\nTag files in your commands using the `@[filename]` syntax:\n\n```bash\n: Review this code @[src/main.rs]\n: Explain the configuration in @[config.yaml]\n```\n\n**Interactive Selection**: Type `@` and press `TAB` to search and select files interactively using fuzzy finder.\n\n### Conversation Continuity\n\nCommands within the same session maintain context:\n\n```bash\n# First command\n: My project uses React and TypeScript\n\n# Second command (remembers previous context)\n: How can I optimize the build process?\n```\n\nThe plugin automatically manages conversation IDs to maintain context across related commands.\n\n### Command Naming\n\nShell commands should follow the **Object-Action** format.\n\nExamples:\n- `:provider-login`\n- `:sync-status`\n\nFor backward compatibility, `:login` remains available as an alias for `:provider-login`.\n\n### Session Management\n\n#### Starting New Sessions\n\nClear the current conversation context and start fresh:\n\n```bash\n:new\n# or use the alias\n:n\n```\n\nThis will:\n\n- Clear the current conversation ID\n- Show the banner with helpful information\n- Reset the session state\n- Display a confirmation message with timestamp\n\n#### System Information\n\nView system and project information:\n\n```bash\n:info\n# or use the alias\n:i\n```\n\nThis displays:\n\n- System information\n- Project details\n- Current configuration\n\n- Current configuration\n\n#### Switching Conversations\n\nBrowse and switch between conversations interactively:\n\n```bash\n:conversation\n# or use the alias\n:c\n```\n\nThis will display an interactive list of all conversations with preview, allowing you to select and switch.\n\nSwitch to a specific conversation by ID:\n\n```bash\n:conversation <conversation_id>\n```\n\nToggle between current and previous conversation (like `cd -`):\n\n```bash\n:conversation -\n# or\n:c -\n```\n\nThe plugin remembers your previous conversation, allowing you to quickly toggle back and forth. This works just like `cd -` in your shell, and **also works with `:new`** - when you start a new conversation, you can toggle back to your previous one.\n\nIf there's no previous conversation tracked (e.g., first time using the plugin), `:c -` will show the conversation list popup, allowing you to select a conversation.\n\nThis is useful when:\n- You need to temporarily check another conversation and come back\n- You're comparing or referencing information between two conversations\n- You want to quickly switch context between related tasks\n- You started a new conversation but want to reference the previous one\n\n#### Cloning Conversations\n\nCreate a copy of an existing conversation with interactive selection:\n\n```bash\n:clone\n```\n\nThis will:\n- Display an interactive list of all conversations with preview\n- Allow you to select a conversation to clone\n- Create a new conversation with the same content\n- Automatically switch to the cloned conversation\n- Show the cloned conversation content and details\n\nYou can also clone a specific conversation by providing its ID:\n\n```bash\n:clone <conversation_id>\n```\n\nThis is useful when you want to:\n- Create a backup before making significant changes\n- Start a new conversation branch from an existing context\n- Experiment with different approaches while preserving the original\n\n#### Session Status\n\nThe plugin automatically displays session information including:\n- Conversation ID when starting new sessions\n- Active agent information\n- New session confirmations with timestamps\n\n## Syntax Highlighting\n\nThe plugin provides visual feedback through syntax highlighting:\n\n- **Tagged Files** (`@[filename]`): Displayed in **green bold**\n- **Agent Commands** (`:agent`): Agent names in **yellow bold**\n- **Command Text**: Remaining text in **white bold**\n\n## Configuration\n\nCustomize the plugin behavior by setting these variables before loading the plugin:\n\n```bash\n# Custom forge binary location\nexport FORGE_BIN=\"/path/to/custom/forge\"\n```\n\n### Available Configuration Variables\n\n- `FORGE_BIN`: Path to the forge executable (default: `forge`)\n- `FORGE_EDITOR`: then\n        # Switch to conversation and track in history\n        _forge_switch_conversation \"$conversation_id\"\n        \n        # Show conversation content\n        echo\n        _forge_exec conversation show \"$conversation_id\"\n        \n        # Show conversation info\n        _forge_exec conversation info \"$conversation_id\"\n        \n        # Print log about conversation switching\n        _forge_log success \"Switched to conversation \\033[1m${conversation_id}\\033[0m\"\n    fi\n}\n\n# Action handler: Clone conversation\nfunction _forge_action_clone() {\n    local input_text=\"$1\"\n    local clone_target=\"$input_text\"\n    \n    echo\n    \n    # Handle explicit clone target if provided\n    if [[ -n \"$clone_target\" ]]; 419279 write(6, "#!/usr/bin/env zsh\n\n# Conversation management action handlers\n# \n# Features:\n# - :conversation          - List and switch conversations (with interactive picker)\n# - :conversation <id>     - Switch to specific conversation by ID\n# - :conversation -        - Toggle between current and previous conversation (like cd -)\n# - :clone                 - Clone current or selected conversation\n# - :clone <id>            - Clone specific conversation by ID\n# - :copy                  - Copy last assistant message to OS clipboard as raw markdown\n# - :rename <name>         - Rename the current conversation\n# - :conversation-rename   - Rename a conversation (interactive picker)\n# - :conversation-rename <id> <name> - Rename specific conversation by ID\n#\n# Helper Functions:\n# - _forge_switch_conversation <id>  - Switch to a conversation and track previous\n# - _forge_clear_conversation        - Clear conversation and save as previous\n\n# Helper function to switch to a conversation and track previous (like cd -)\nfunction _forge_switch_conversation() {\n    local new_conversation_id=\"$1\"\n    \n    # Only update previous if we're switching to a different conversation\n    if [[ -n \"$_FORGE_CONVERSATION_ID\" && \"$_FORGE_CONVERSATION_ID\" != \"$new_conversation_id\" ]]; then\n        # Save current as previous\n        _FORGE_PREVIOUS_CONVERSATION_ID=\"$_FORGE_CONVERSATION_ID\"\n    fi\n    \n    # Set the new conversation as active\n    _FORGE_CONVERSATION_ID=\"$new_conversation_id\"\n}\n\n# Helper function to reset/clear conversation and track previous (like cd -)\nfunction _forge_clear_conversation() {\n    # Save current as previous before clearing\n    if [[ -n \"$_FORGE_CONVERSATION_ID\" ]]; then\n        _FORGE_PREVIOUS_CONVERSATION_ID=\"$_FORGE_CONVERSATION_ID\"\n    fi\n    \n    # Clear the current conversation\n    _FORGE_CONVERSATION_ID=\"\"\n}\n\n# Action handler: List/switch conversations\nfunction _forge_action_conversation() {\n    local input_text=\"$1\"\n    \n    echo\n    \n    # Handle toggling to previous conversation (like cd -)\n    if [[ \"$input_text\" == \"-\" ]]; then\n        _forge_clone_and_switch \"$clone_target\"\n        return 0\n    fi\n    \n    # Use Rust's built-in conversation picker\n    local conversation_id\n    conversation_id=$(_forge_select conversation)\n    \n    if [[ -n \"$conversation_id\" ]]; then\n        _forge_clone_and_switch \"$conversation_id\"\n    fi\n}\n\n# Action handler: Copy last assistant message to OS clipboard as raw markdown\n# Usage: :copy\nfunction _forge_action_copy() {\n    echo\n\n    if [[ -z \"$_FORGE_CONVERSATION_ID\" ]]; Handling\n\n## 1. Natural Language\n\nConvert user requirements into executable commands.\n\n_Example 1:_\n- Input: \"List all files\"\n- Output: {\"command\": \"ls -la\"}\n\n_Example 2:_\n- Input: \"Find all Python files in current directory\"\n- Output: {\"command\": \"find . -name \\\"*.py\\\"\"}\n\n_Example 3:_\n- Input: \"Show disk usage in human readable format\"\n- Output: {\"command\": \"df -h\"}\n\n## 2. Invalid/Malformed Commands\n\nCorrect malformed or incomplete commands. Auto-correct typos and assume the most likely intention.\n\n_Example 1:_\n- Input: \"get status\"\n- Output: {\"command\": \"git status\"}\n\n_Example 2:_\n- Input: \"docker ls\"\n- Output: {\"command\": \"docker ps\"}\n\n_Example 3:_\n- Input: \"npm start server\"\n- Output: {\"command\": \"npm start\"}\n\n_Example 4:_\n- Input: \"git pul origin mster\"\n- Output: {\"command\": \"git pull origin master\"}\n\n## 3. Vague/Unclear Input\n\nFor vague requests, provide the most helpful general-purpose command.\n\n_Example 1:_\n- Input: \"help me\" or \"im confused\"\n- Output: {\"command\": \"pwd && ls -la\"}\n\n_Example 2:_\n- Input: \"check stuff\"\n- Output: {\"command\": \"ls -lah\"}\n\n## 4. Edge Cases\n\n### Empty or Whitespace-Only Input\n- Input: \"\" or \" \"\n- Output: {\"command\": \"\"}\n\n### Gibberish/Random Characters\n- Input: \"fjdkslajfkdlsajf\" or \"asdfghjkl\"\n- Output: {\"command\": \"\"}\n\n### Only Numbers or Symbols\n- Input: \"123456789\" or \"!@#$%\"\n- Output: {\"command\": \"\"}\n\n### Emojis Only\n- Input: \"\360\237\232\200\360\237\224\245\360\237\222\257\"\n- Output: {\"command\": \"echo \\\"\360\237\232\200\360\237\224\245\360\237\222\257\\\"\"}\n\n### Injection Attempts (SQL, XSS, etc.)\n- Input: \"SELECT _ FROM users; DROP TABLE--\"\n- Output: {\"command\": \"echo \\\"SELECT _ FROM users; DROP TABLE--\\\"\"}\n\n## 5. Dangerous Operations\n\nFor obviously destructive operations, provide a safe alternative or clear warning.\n\n_Example 1:_\n- Input: \"sudo rm -rf /\"\n- Output: {\"command\": \"echo \\\"\360\237\232\253 Refusing to run: deleting root (/) would destroy the system.\\\"\"}\n\n_Example 2:_\n- Input: \"rm -rf \\\"\"\n- Output: {\"command\": \"echo \\\"\342\232\240\357\270\217 This would delete everything in the current directory.
